original_question: For an almost-complex manifold M, are the dimensions h^{p,q} defined as the kernel dimensions of the d-bar Laplacian independent of the choice of Hermitian metric, and if not, is there a replacement notion of h^{p,q} depending only on the almost-complex structure that extends Dolbeault cohomology from the integrable case?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 20 (Kodaira-Spencer): Dolbeault cohomology for almost complex manifolds.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the two-part question in Problem 20: whether the numbers h^{p,q} coming from the d-bar Laplacian depend on the chosen Hermitian structure, and, if they do, whether one can replace them by numbers depending only on the almost-complex structure and recovering the usual complex-manifold h^{p,q} in the integrable case.
missing_details: The local context in Section 5 is a closed almost-complex manifold; compactness/closedness is part of what makes the kernel dimensions finite-dimensional.
The paper first fixes an almost Hermitian structure compatible with the almost-complex structure J; it is not an arbitrary Riemannian metric.
The relevant forms are complex-valued differential forms decomposed into (p,q)-types via TM ⊗_R C = T^{1,0}M ⊕ T^{0,1}M.
The operator \bar\partial is defined as the component of d that raises q by one (and similarly \partial raises p by one).
In the non-integrable case, d has additional Nijenhuis-tensor terms, so \bar\partial^2 need not vanish on all forms; this is why the problem is not simply to define ordinary \bar\partial-cohomology.

The Laplacian in question should be written explicitly as \Box_{\bar\partial} = \bar\partial^*\bar\partial + \bar\partial\bar\partial^*, where \bar\partial^* is the L^2-adjoint with respect to the chosen Hermitian structure.
The paper denotes by H^{p,q} the kernel of \Box_{\bar\partial} on the space A^{p,q}(M) of (p,q)-forms, and by h^{p,q} its complex dimension.
The quantifier is over each bidegree (p,q), implicitly with 0 ≤ p,q ≤ n when dim_R M = 2n.

To be fully paper-faithful, the replacement asked for is 'some other definition of the h^{p,q}' depending only on J; the paper does not itself insist that this replacement must already be formulated as a full cohomology theory.
In the integrable case, the recovery statement should be phrased as agreement with the usual h^{p,q} of a compact complex manifold, which are the Dolbeault-cohomology dimensions.
refined_question: Let (M^{2n}, J) be a closed almost-complex manifold. For each bidegree (p,q) with 0 ≤ p,q ≤ n and for each Hermitian structure compatible with J, let A^{p,q}(M) be the space of complex-valued (p,q)-forms, let \bar\partial be the component of d that raises q by one, let \bar\partial^* be its L^2-adjoint, and define the d-bar Laplacian by \Box_{\bar\partial} = \bar\partial^*\bar\partial + \bar\partial\bar\partial^*. If H^{p,q} := ker(\Box_{\bar\partial}|_{A^{p,q}(M)}) and h^{p,q} := dim_C H^{p,q}, are the numbers h^{p,q} independent of the chosen Hermitian structure? If not, can one give another definition of numbers h^{p,q}(J), depending only on the almost-complex structure J, that in the integrable case coincide with the usual h^{p,q} of a compact complex manifold?
justification: This is the exact problem your draft is aiming at. In the introduction, Kotschick lists Problem 20 as one of the problems that remain essentially open. In Section 5 he introduces the almost-complex decomposition of forms, defines the d-bar Laplacian from \bar\partial and its adjoint, defines H^{p,q} as its kernel and h^{p,q} as its dimension, and then states Problem 20 in essentially the same two-part form as your draft. I did not broaden the question to index-theoretic invariance, because the very next remark says that Atiyah-Singer only gives metric-independence of the fixed-p index of \bar\partial + \bar\partial^*, whereas Problem 20 concerns the individual numbers h^{p,q} defined via the d-bar Laplacian.
